title: NovaTrust POC — Infosec Audit Companion (working notes)
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc is a living workpad for the NovaTrust POC (finance customer) — capture of infosec questions, artifacts we can provide, gaps to remediate before the customer audit-readiness call, and runbook-level notes for the engineering lead coordinating uploads.

High level customer ask (TL;DR):
- NovaTrust wants to validate Redwood Private VPC deployment for an LLM inference flow that processes KYC PII and transaction metadata.
- Primary concerns: data residency, customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS), audit log fidelity, network isolation, and rollout rollback/incident response.
- Deliverables requested for POC review: control mapping + evidence bundle, sample logs, network diagram, KMS proof, runtime config, and a short security Q&A they can attach to their internal audit.

Assumptions (clarify before packaging):
- POC environment is a dedicated VPC in us-east1 and eu-west1 (dual-region).
- Customer will provide a list of sample payloads (redacted) for synthetic runs — we will not use production customer data.
- NovaTrust requires that keys be customer-managed (we support BYOK integrations).

Quick meeting notes (2025-09-30 workshop):
Attendees: Maya Chen (RDI), Liam O'Connor (RDI), Priya Nair (RDI - solutions), Nora Patel (NovaTrust security), Tom Berger (NovaTrust infra)
- Nora walked through their internal control set mapped to SOC2/ISO.
- Asked for 3rd-party attestation for HSM vendor and confirmation of key rotation windows.
- Concern: prefix caching and KV leakage if model cache persisted between tenants. We demoed per-tenant isolation and cache purging API.
Action items from workshop:
1) Provide network diagram with subnets, firewall rules, and Cloud NAT details (owner: Diego Ramos) — due 2025-10-07
2) Export sample audit logs (token-level latency masked) for a 24h window — owner: Maya Chen — due 2025-10-05
3) Prepare KMS BYOK PoC notes and KMS access policy snippet (owner: Priya Nair) — due 2025-10-04
4) Draft short answers to their 40-question infosec spreadsheet (owner: Maya) — initial pass due 2025-10-02

Artifact checklist (current status) — quick table (text):
- Network diagram: Needed by auditor; STATUS: in_progress; GAP: missing Cloud Armor rule numbers; EVIDENCE NAME: nt_network_diagram_v1.png
- KMS (BYOK) configuration snapshot: Needed; STATUS: ready (redacted); GAP: need HSM attestation PDF from vendor; EVIDENCE NAME: nt_kms_byok_snapshot.pdf
- IAM role list for deployment service accounts: Needed; STATUS: ready; GAP: annotate which roles are customer-supplied vs Redwood-managed; EVIDENCE NAME: nt_iam_roles.csv
- Sample audit logs (ingest + inference events): Needed; STATUS: collecting; GAP: scrub PII; EVIDENCE NAME: nt_audit_logs_sample.jsonl
- Runtime config (quantization + batching policy): Useful for performance & risk analysis; STATUS: draft; EVIDENCE NAME: nt_runtime_config.txt
- Data flow diagram (end-to-end): Needed; STATUS: draft; GAP: show encryption-in-transit arrows; EVIDENCE NAME: nt_data_flow.svg
- Pen test summary (redacted): Optional but requested; STATUS: vendor_pending; EVIDENCE NAME: pentest_summary_redacted.pdf
- SOC2 excerpt (applicable scope): Optional; STATUS: available; EVIDENCE NAME: redwood_soc2_scope_excerpt.pdf

Suggested short Q&A wording (snippets to drop into customer spreadsheet):
Q: Where does customer data at rest reside?
A: Customer data for this POC is stored in NovaTrust's dedicated object storage within the deployed VPC subnet in the selected region(s). Redwood's runtime mounts ephemeral caches on the compute nodes; long-term persistence of PII is disabled by default.

Q: Who manages encryption keys?
A: Keys are customer-managed. We support KMS integrations and BYOK; the control plane stores only references to key identifiers. For customers requiring HSM-backed keys, we support external HSM attestation documents and KMS claim proofs.

Q: Can you prove logs are immutable for the review window?
A: We can export signed log bundles with timestamps and sequence checksums. For the POC we will provide a 24h signed audit log sample with sequence checksums and a simple verification script.

Gap notes and mitigations (short):
- HSM attestation: vendor is in-process; escalate to partnerships for expedited attestation paperwork.
- Cache purge automation: create a small script that calls the per-tenant cache-flush API and return HTTP 200 artifacts to show purge completion. Owner: engineering (serving-runtime).
- Pen test redaction: coordinate with vendor to produce a redacted executive summary suitable for customer review.

Packaging guidance for the evidence bundle (how I plan to assemble files):
- Top-level README (nt_readme.txt) describing scope, environment IDs, and redaction policy.
- artifacts/ directory: diagrams, config snippets, logs (redacted), policy snippets (IAM/KMS), attestation PDFs.
- control-mapping.csv: two columns (customer_control_id, redwood_evidence_file_name) — simple CSV so auditors can map quickly.
- short-qa.pdf: concise answers to their 40 Qs (one-page executive summary + appendix with longer answers).

Suggested content for README (short):
- POC name: NovaTrust POC
- Date range: 2025-09-28 to 2025-10-04
- Environment tags: nt-poc-us, nt-poc-eu
- Contact: Maya Chen (mchen@redwood.ai), Security lead: Liam O'Connor
- Redaction note: All PII has been redacted from logs. We provide a redaction audit trail in artifacts/redaction_manifest.txt

Risk register (short bullets):
- Risk: accidental leak of redacted sample containing hashed user IDs. Mitigation: double-redaction + small team review.
- Risk: HSM attestation delay. Mitigation: provide alternate KMS screenshot + vendor contract excerpt while final attestation arrives.
- Risk: customer wants continuous log forwarding (SLA concern). Mitigation: propose a 30-day pilot with retention policy and options for log-forwarding into customer SIEM.

Templates / copy snippets (quick internal use):
- Email subject: "NovaTrust POC — Infosec evidence bundle (initial)"
- Email body (short): "Hi Nora — attached is the initial evidence bundle for the NovaTrust POC. See nt_readme.txt for scope. We have highlighted a few open items in the control-mapping.csv. Please let us know if you need additional context or a live walkthrough. — Maya"

Next steps (immediate, top of backlog):
- Diego: finalize network diagram and export firewall rule set (2025-10-07)
- Maya: finish answering the 40-question spreadsheet and attach short-qa.pdf (2025-10-02)
- Priya: create KMS BYOK notes and include an example IAM policy snippet (2025-10-04)
- Liam: request HSM attestation from vendor partnership team and share ETA (2025-10-06)

Notes to self / miscellaneous: 
- Keep evidence filenames short and stable (no spaces).
- When exporting logs use UTC timestamps and include timezone metadata in README.
- Mark any files that contain even redacted identifiers with a warning header so auditors know what was redacted and why.

Revision history:
- 2025-09-12: created initial outline (Maya)
- 2025-09-30: workshop capture + action items added (Maya)
- 2025-10-03: artifact checklist updated after engineering sync (Maya, Diego)

End of workpad — treat this as the single source for bundle assembly until we push a finalized packet to nt_evidence_v1.zip
